subject: HarborBridge — intermittent connection stutter & elevated 5xx rate
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice@harborbridge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: engineering@harborbridge.com
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: High error rate / latency spike affecting checkout - urgent

Hi Markus —

We’re seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and 5xx responses from Redwood for our checkout path since ~08:40 PST. Traffic is normal on our side; traces show repeated connection stalls and DNS lookup delays before the SDK attempts a retry. Impact: ~25% of requests returning 5xx and median p95 latency up from 120ms to ~1.8s. This is affecting a subset of regions (us-west primarily) and causing checkout failures for customers.

We’ve attached a few sample traces and a pcap. Can you open an incident? We need an executive update — HarborBridge is asking for an ETA on a mitigation and any temporary workarounds we should apply.

- Alice
VP Engineering, HarborBridge
Attachments: trace-20281116-harborbridge.pcap (pcap), sample-log-snippets.txt (text)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice@harborbridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:15:23 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency spike affecting checkout - urgent

Alice — thanks for the heads-up and the traces. I’ve opened an incident (INC-HB-4302) and pulled in the network and infra on-call. Vanessa / Rishi, can you triage networking + peering, DNS, and proxy behavior for HarborBridge traffic (account: HB-4302)?

Actions I’ve started:
- Created incident bridge and posted your attachments to the incident folder.
- Notified leadership (Grace) for executive visibility.
- Asking HarborBridge to temporarily route critical checkout traffic to us-east if feasible — can be a short-term mitigant.

Alice — we’ll aim to have an initial update within 30 minutes. Please keep sample traces coming (request IDs + timestamps are most helpful).

— Markus
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: hb-quick-fix-runbook.pdf (runbook)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:45:10 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency spike affecting checkout - urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed repeated BGP route churn on the peering fabric for the HarborBridge prefix set in us-west-2 starting 08:36 PST. Multiple route withdraws -> re-advertisements traced to a transit partner — correlates with the timing in Alice's traces.
- DNS: our resolver logs show elevated NXDOMAIN and timeouts for HarborBridge's customer hostnames from a subset of egress nodes. TTLs are normal but we see increased lookup retries from the proxy layer.
- Proxy/firewall: policy check latency spiked on several proxies handling that egress cluster; connection setup times (SYN->ACK) were elevated.

Immediate mitigations proposed:
1) Move HarborBridge traffic bound for checkout to alternate peering (peer-set B) to avoid the flapping transit for the next 60–90 minutes.
2) Temporarily increase DNS cache TTL on the egress cluster to reduce lookup pressure (low risk for HB domain set).
3) Apply a high-priority bypass rule on the proxy for HarborBridge's checkout prefix to skip deep inspection for 30m.

I’ll coordinate with the transit partner and prepare a short config push. If we do the routing cutover, we should see tail latency improve in the next 3–7 minutes.

— Vanessa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: handoff-map.png (diagram of current peering vs alternate peer-set)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice@harborbridge.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 09:53:05 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency spike affecting checkout - urgent

Alice — update for exec stakeholders: Vanessa identified transient peering churn and a correlated DNS/proxy amplification that is driving the tail latency and 5xxs. We are initiating an outbound peering switch to an alternate transit (peer-set B) and will apply a short-term proxy bypass for checkout traffic. Expected user-facing improvement: p95/p99 latency should return towards baseline within 3–10 minutes post-cutover.

Grace — looping you in so we have exec visibility; I’ll post a short status update to the incident page and flag if we need a formal customer credit or expedited postmortem.

Alice — can you confirm whether HarborBridge can hold non-critical deploys for the next 2 hours and whether you can switch critical checkout traffic to us-east if we ask? Either helps as a fallback.

— Markus
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice@harborbridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 02:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency spike affecting checkout - incident resolved, next steps

Alice — final update: we implemented the alternate peering cutover at 09:58 PST and applied the temporary proxy bypass and TTL increase. Observations:
- Error rate dropped from 25% -> 1.2% within 4 minutes of cutover.
- p95 latency returned to ~140ms, p99 to ~420ms across affected nodes.
- No customer-visible side effects reported after mitigation window.

Actions / next steps:
- We’ll keep the alternate peering active for 6 hours while the transit partner stabilizes.
- Full postmortem and timeline (INC-HB-4302) will be shared within 48 hours and will include recommended permanent mitigations (improved peer health monitoring, stronger route dampening, and a refined proxy fast-path for checkout flows).
- I attached the quick-fix runbook and the capture we used for triage.

If HarborBridge wants a technical readout for your ops/infra team, Vanessa can run a 30-minute sync tomorrow.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll follow up with a formal postmortem link.

— Markus
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachments: hb-quick-fix-runbook.pdf, trace-20281116-harborbridge.pcap
